items.title: Alrededor de 2.000 espectadores arropan al Athletic en Lezama
items.description: El Athletic ha recibido el calor de la afición en el regreso al trabajo en Lezama después de la derrota cosechada el viernes en San Mamés ante el Espanyol. El club ha organizado el segundo entrenamiento a puerta abierta de la temporada después del llevado a cabo el pasado 6 de octubre, cuando la asistencia fue de aproximadamente 500 espectadores en un día laborable y con los más pequeños en sus colegios. “Quizás no fue el mejor día y lo tendremos en cuenta”, reconoció Terzic. Hoy la asistencia se ha acercado a lo esperado en estas ocasiones, con alrededor de 2.000 aficionados en el campo 2 de Lezama, donde juega el Femenino y el Bilbao Athletic. Una de las gradas laterales estaba casi llena, lo mismo que la que está ubicada detrás de una de las porterías.

items.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
items.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change“If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis. Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears.In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided, Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. items.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
items.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoidedSign up for our free newsletter hereIn as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter.Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0. Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023. Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

items.title: El Barça ya vuela a Bakú, su viaje más largo en la historia de la Champions
items.description: Dos veces en menos de un año tuvo que viajar el Barça de Pep Guardiola a la localidad rusa de Kazán, en la República de Tartaristán, para enfrentarse al Rubin. El 4 de noviembre de 2009, el equipo azulgrana no pasó del 0-0 en el Grupo F de la fase inicial de la Champions League 2009-10, y el 29 de septiembre de 2010 también se tuvo que conformar con un 1-1 (gol de David Villa de penalti) en el Grupo D de una Champions League 2010-11 que acabó conquistando en Wembley. Aquellos dos desplazamientos de 3.725 kilómetros suponían el récord de distancia del FC Barcelona en la Champions League, también en competición europea. El viaje a Bakú (Azerbaiyán) para el Sabah-Barça del miércoles (18.45 horas) lo supera: 3.970 kilómetros y casi seis horas de vuelo. La expedición del Barça ya vuela desde las 13 horas.

In the end, though, the best news of the night was that Saïd El Mala, the star of the visitors, Köln, who had scored a jaw-dropping consolation goal at the same stadium in spring, fluffed a far easier chance in the closing stages that would have condemned the champions to defeat.The word crisis is rampantly overused in sport, but this was the weekend Bayern’s injury troubles reached critical mass. With Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismaël Saibari already missing, their talisman Harry Kane had his game curtailed after 20 minutes and by the time the second half had begun, they’d lost Michael Olise too. items.description: El Deportivo Alavés derrotó este sábado al Deportivo de La Coruña por 3-1 en Mendizorroza para escalar hasta la novena posición de LaLiga gracias a los goles de Ángel Pérez, Lucas Boyé y Denis Suárez. Precisamente el ex del Celta de Vigo, quien mantiene una gran rivalidad con el Dépor por su sentimiento 'celeste', no dudó en mandarle un recado al conjunto gallego al término del partido. "Teníamos muchas ganas de este partido, yo especialmente. items.title: Alivio con Aramburu tras retirarse llorando: se descarta una lesión de gravedad
items.description: El cuerpo técnico de la Real Sociedad respira algo más aliviado tras el susto protagonizado por Jon Mikel Aramburu en el tramo final del encuentro ante el Racing de Santander. Según informa el club, las primeras exploraciones médicas realizadas ayer mismo tras el pitido final en El Sardinero descartan una lesión grave del lateral venezolano. Todo queda reducido a una fortísima contusión en la zona de la cadera fruto de un duro impacto de Íñigo Vicente, una acción muy al límite que dejó al defensa llorando sobre el césped y obligó al cuerpo técnico a pedirle que abandonara el terreno de juego en el tiempo de descuento, dejando al equipo con diez futbolistas al no poder siquiera mantenerse erguido ni tirar la línea del fuera de juego.

items.title: Un récord sin premio: los 31 disparos de la Real Sociedad que murieron en El Sardinero
items.description: La derrota de la Real Sociedad en El Sardinero dejó una sensación amarga desde todos los prismas. El equipo de Pellegrino Matarazzo sometió al Racing a un bombardeo constante durante los noventa minutos y disparó un total de 31 veces, una auténtica barbaridad para un encuentro de Primera División. Habitualmente, el conjunto donostiarra se mueve en una horquilla de entre 15 y 20 remates por partido -registros ya de por sí elevados y situados por encima de la media de LaLiga-, pero en Santander pulverizó cualquier precedente de la temporada. Hasta la fecha, su tope estaba fijado en los 21 lanzamientos frente a Valencia, Málaga y Deportivo, diez por debajo del vendaval ofensivo desatado este domingo en territorio cántabro.

items.title: "Me voy a ir con penalti y tarjeta roja por DOGSO"
items.description: La contundente victoria anoche del Atlético de Madrid en Getafe por 0-3 tuvo además una intervención desde el VAR. Fue en los instantes finales y cuando los rojiblancos ya ganaban dos cero. Un empujón de Djene a Sorloth dentro del área cuando ya encaraba a David Soria que el colegiado Jesús Gil Manzano no indicó inicialmente como pena máxima. Es entonces cuando fue avisado desde el VAR por Rubén Ávalos Barrera: "Jesús, te recomiendo una revisión para que valores un potencial penalti. Avísame cuando estés en la pantalla por favor": Camino al monitor se escucha al colegiado internacional: "Controlarme los banquillos, aquí yo Lupe (en referencia a la asistente Guadalupe Porras)" y es la asistente internacional femenina la que trata de poner calma: "Por favor, por favor. Vale, ya está, vale. Dejamos trabajar, dejamos trabajar, dejamos trabajar" para que dejen espacio en el monitor.

items.title: ‘Haaland must be worried’: Thierno Barry’s rise has David Moyes purring
items.description: Everton striker has worked hard to find his scoring touch after admitting he hit ‘rock bottom’ at times last seasonA most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. The rise of Thierno Barry may have surprised even the man himself but stands as a fitting reward for single-minded perseverance and the refusal to quit.“Fabulous” was David Moyes’s take on Barry’s last performance for Everton, when a double against Coventry took the striker to 10 goals for the season in all competitions and his team temporarily up to fifth. It was high praise indeed from a manager who does not dispense tributes freely, and can appear to be on the French forward’s case constantly, but was no more than Barry deserved for a display that also featured an assist for Everton’s third goal of the night. His six Premier League goals leave him joint third alongside Evanilson of Bournemouth and Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson. Continue reading...

items.title: El Athletic abre las puertas de Lezama a la afición
items.description: El Athletic regresa hoy al trabajo en las instalaciones de Lezama (17.30 horas) después de la jornada de descanso disfrutada ayer y lo hace con público en las gradas por segunda vez en la temporada. El club ha programado un entrenamiento a puerta abierta. Habrá que comprobar la respuesta del público en una día laborable, aunque en esta ocasión el horario puede permitir a los escolares acercarse a Lezama una vez acabadas sus clases. El otro, celebrado el martes 6 de octubre, registró una baja asistencia. Alrededor de 500 espectadores presenciaron la sesión en el campo 2. “Quizás no fue el mejor día y lo tendremos en cuenta”, reconoció Terzic. Al igual que en la sesión anterior, será necesario reservar una entrada gratuita.

items.title: El Athletic abre el candado de su propia portería
items.description: Edin Terzic recordó el viernes que su equipo no ha ganado ninguno de los dos últimos partidos. Su equipo fue algo mejor que el conjunto rojillo y también mereció al menos un empate contra los pericos por el empuje demostrado en la última media hora, pero la falta de pegada arriba con aquella ocasión de Iñaki Williams a pase de su hermano en la primera mitad y sobre todo la falta de finura en los últimos metros para crear ocasiones claras acabaron por sentenciar a los leones. items.title: Lionel Messi’s incident revives Cristiano Ronaldo’s 2024 controversy as Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois calls for red card
items.description:
Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have both experienced moments when their on-field reactions sparked debate over how referees handle confrontations involving soccer's biggest stars. 
Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have both experienced moments when their on-field reactions sparked debate over how referees handle confrontations involving soccer’s biggest stars. Messi’s latest controversy has brought fresh scrutiny to Inter Miami’s MLS Cup playoff campaign, with a rival coach questioning a major decision that could have consequences for the Argentine’s team.



The incident occurred during a difficult evening for the defending champions, who suffered a damaging defeat against Columbus Crew. While the result put Miami on the brink of elimination, the confrontation involving Messi quickly became one of the biggest talking points after the final whistle.



Miami entered its first-round meeting with Columbus on Saturday hoping to begin its title defence with a victory. Messi had received the MLS Golden Boot before kick-off, becoming the first player to win the award in consecutive seasons, but the celebrations soon gave way to frustration.



The Crew took the lead in the ninth minute after goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair brought down Gonzalo Tapia inside the penalty area. The Chilean forward converted the resulting spot-kick, while goalkeeper Patrick Schulte produced several important saves to keep Messi and Miami at bay.









The hosts’ situation deteriorated further in the 36th minute when Gonzalo Lujan received his second yellow card for a late challenge on Steven Moreira. Miami was left with 10 players for the remainder of the contest, giving Columbus a significant advantage.



Messi clashes with Tapia as tensions boil over



The most controversial moment arrived during first-half stoppage time, when Messi and Tapia became involved in an argument near the touchline. As the Argentine attempted to take a quick throw-in, the Columbus forward stood close to him and appeared to obstruct the restart.



Messi reacted by pushing the ball into Tapia’s face before throwing it towards his opponent’s head from close range. The Chilean went to ground, prompting protests from Columbus players and a heated exchange between members of both teams.



Lionel Messi takes a throw-in off Gonzalo Tapia's face pic.twitter.com/jX3tTuojHe— Tom Bogert (@tombogert) November 22, 2026 



Referee Allen Chapman showed both players a yellow card, allowing Messi to remain on the pitch. The decision immediately divided opinion, particularly because Miami was already trailing and playing with 10 men.



Columbus coach questions referee’s decision



Columbus head coach Laurent Courtois was particularly unhappy that Messi avoided a sending-off. The Crew manager believed the Argentine should have received a red card for his actions against Tapia. 



“Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said after the match. “It’s just really sad.” Chapman subsequently defended his decision when questioned by a pool reporter. “The force used was negligible, and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct,” the referee explained.



Laurent Courtois sobre la tarjeta amarilla a Messi:"Todo el mundo sabe que eso era más que una amarilla"Además, le consulté si espera una revisión por parte de MLS.#InterMiamiCF #Crew96 pic.twitter.com/M4Oi3BeqwK— José Armando (@Jarm21) November 22, 2026 



The distinction was central to the disciplinary debate, with Major League Soccer’s competition guidelines defining violent conduct as the use of excessive force or brutality when a player is not challenging for the ball. The Athletic refereeing expert Graham Scott reportedly argued that a red card would have been the more defensible decision, believing the contact was deliberate and excessive.



Why Messi’s incident recalls Ronaldo’s 2024 red card



The confrontation brought back memories of Cristiano Ronaldo’s straight red card against Al-Hilal in the Saudi Super Cup semi-final on April 8, 2024. The Al-Nassr forward became involved in a physical altercation with defender Saud Abdulhamid during a dispute over a throw-in, responding with aggressive physical contact that sent his opponent to the ground.



The referee dismissed the Portuguese for violent conduct, and Al-Nassr eventually lost 2-1. The incident resurfaced online alongside footage of Messi’s confrontation with Tapia, with fans debating whether the two superstars had been treated consistently. There were clear similarities in the circumstances, as the trigger was almost identical.



Many Ronaldo fans will swear this is not a Red card,That the system is always against him https://t.co/MBIcjQQ6bW pic.twitter.com/KPjg5RWa7p— Metua Metua (@Metuametua29) November 22, 2026 



In both cases, an opponent stood close and actively impeded a quick throw-in, a common tactic to waste time or disrupt momentum. Players are required to retreat a reasonable distance, yet enforcement is often inconsistent. What’s more, both Messi and Ronaldo, known more for brilliance than volatility, lost composure in the heat of a competitive fixture when their team was struggling. 



These are not random acts of aggression but responses to perceived gamesmanship. The opponent went down in each case, leading to questions of whether the contact was violent enough for a red card. The Argentine used the ball; the Portuguese used his body.



Lionel Messi drilled Gonzalo Tapia in the head with this throw-in pic.twitter.com/TEwPTFvMSK— Jomboy Media (@JomboyMedia) November 22, 2026 



While the situations rhyme, they are not identical. Messi directed a ball at an opponent’s face from very short range; Ronaldo made direct physical contact with his body. Laws of the Game treat excessive force or violent conduct more severely when it involves striking or headbutting than when the object is a ball, though intent and force still matter.

items.title: Lionel Messi’s USA era draws fresh attention after Son Heung-Min agrees with Thomas Muller as MLS comes under fire over one major problem
items.description:
As the league continues to grow and welcome established international names, questions remain over whether its competitive structure provides the intensity players are accustomed to in Europe. 
Lionel Messi‘s arrival in the United States has helped Major League Soccer attract unprecedented attention, with fellow stars Son Heung-Min and Thomas Muller also bringing considerable experience from European soccer. However, as the league continues to grow and welcome established international names, questions remain over whether its competitive structure provides the intensity players are accustomed to in Europe.



Son has now added his voice to a debate started by Muller, agreeing with the Vancouver Whitecaps forward’s assessment of the differences between MLS and Europe’s leading competitions. Both players have experienced soccer at the highest level, making their comments particularly significant as the American league looks to strengthen its global reputation.



Muller, who joined the Vancouver Whitecaps in 2025 after a distinguished career with Bayern Munich, recently discussed the challenges of comparing MLS with European leagues. The German World Cup winner suggested that the American competition operates under a different level of pressure because of its unique structure. Speaking to Global News, the German explained: “It’s difficult to compare because of the system. There is no relegation, there is no big pressure.



“There is, ‘Oh yeah, we do a rebuild.’ Nobody’s happy to lose, but it’s totally different when you fight [against] getting relegated.” He also highlighted the consequences European clubs face when they drop into a lower division, including reduced budgets, potential job losses and uncertainty over players’ contracts. Those stakes, he argued, can dramatically change how teams approach matches, particularly when they face opponents fighting to avoid relegation.



Thomas Müller was not offering criticism just a comparison of systems & the competitive reality in Major League Soccer."There is no big pressure. When you play a bottom of the table team in Europe, they fight for their life." Listen 👇Courtesy of Global News#ProRelForUSA… pic.twitter.com/xFWM0l1NDn— Glenn Crooks (@GlennCrooks) November 19, 2026 



Muller added that MLS teams can sometimes appear more relaxed defensively, describing the approach as “laissez faire”. While he acknowledged that this can produce entertaining attacking soccer, he suggested it can also affect the consistency and intensity of performances across 90 minutes.



Son Heung-Min gives his verdict



The former Tottenham forward was subsequently asked about Muller’s assessment and whether he had experienced similar differences during his time in MLS. Son, who joined LAFC, made his position clear by agreeing with the German’s observations.



“I think Thomas Muller was spot on,” the 34-year-old forward said. “MLS is growing significantly, and big-name players are coming into the league. But sometimes you do feel there’s less pressure because there’s no relegation. You can finish near the bottom and still remain in the league.”



🚨 𝐒𝐎𝐍 𝐇𝐄𝐔𝐍𝐆-𝐌𝐈𝐍: "𝐓𝐇𝐎𝐌𝐀𝐒 𝐌Ü𝐋𝐋𝐄𝐑 𝐖𝐀𝐒 𝐒𝐏𝐎𝐓 𝐎𝐍, 𝐒𝐎𝐌𝐄𝐓𝐈𝐌𝐄𝐒 𝐘𝐎𝐔 𝐅𝐄𝐄𝐋 𝐓𝐇𝐄𝐑𝐄'𝐒 𝐋𝐄𝐒𝐒 𝐏𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐒𝐔𝐑𝐄 𝐈𝐍 𝐌𝐋𝐒 𝐁𝐄𝐂𝐀𝐔𝐒𝐄 𝐓𝐇𝐄𝐑𝐄'𝐒 𝐍𝐎 𝐑𝐄𝐋𝐄𝐆𝐀𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍"❓ "Yesterday, Thomas Müller said there wasn't much…— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) November 22, 2026 



The South Korean international stressed that he enjoys playing in the United States and remains focused on representing LAFC and his country. However, he believes the contrast with European soccer is difficult to ignore.



The absence of relegation at the heart of the debate



Son’s agreement with Muller brings the central issue into focus: MLS does not have a promotion and relegation system, meaning clubs cannot be demoted after finishing at the bottom of the standings. Unlike in the Premier League or Bundesliga, teams struggling throughout the campaign do not face the threat of losing their place in the top division.



The South Korean international drew on his experience in England, where he spent years playing for Tottenham, to explain why the pressure can feel different. “I also played in the Premier League, where you face enormous pressure every single week, sometimes every three days,” he said.



Son Heung-Min of Los Angeles FC



“If you’re not performing, if you’re not playing well, or if your team starts struggling and finds itself near the bottom of the table, you go through a difficult period.” Son believes those survival battles make competition more exciting for both players and supporters.



He also encouraged MLS officials to examine the issue, adding: “I think that makes the competition more fun. I want the best for MLS, and I hope they look into this and perhaps consider making some changes.”



Why MLS is unlikely to introduce relegation



The current system is closely connected to the financial structure of American professional sports. MLS operates through franchises, with owners investing in clubs that benefit from the security of guaranteed participation in the top division.



Introducing relegation could put those investments at risk, potentially reducing franchise values and making the league less attractive to prospective owners. The change would also require significant restructuring and approval from the investors who control the clubs.



Incoming MLS commissioner Larry Berg previously ruled out the prospect of introducing relegation, arguing that it would not help secure investment in stadiums, training facilities and playing squads. His comments underline how difficult it would be for the league to move away from its established model.



Lionel Messi #10 of Inter Miami CF is presented with the 2025 Landon Donovan MLS MVP trophy



Messi’s MLS experience adds another dimension



The debate also raises questions about the balance between competitive pressure and the league’s efforts to create parity. Eighteen of MLS’s 30 teams qualify for the playoffs, giving a large proportion of the competition a chance to win the title even after an inconsistent regular season.



Inter Miami provided a notable example in 2024, when Messi’s team finished with the league’s best regular-season record but was eliminated by Atlanta United in the opening round. Atlanta had finished 34 points behind Miami, demonstrating how the playoff format can produce unexpected outcomes.



Lionel Messi #10 of Inter Miami CF lifts the Champion’s trophy after winning the Audi 2025 MLS Cup Final



MLS also uses mechanisms such as designated player restrictions and the draft to maintain a degree of balance between teams. While those rules can help prevent financial dominance by a small number of clubs, critics argue that the system does not impose enough consequences on underperforming sides.



Neither Son nor Muller has suggested that MLS lacks quality or ambition. Their comments instead highlight a structural difference that could become increasingly important as the league attracts more players with experience of Europe’s most demanding competitions.

items.title: Lamine Yamal breaks La Liga record for all the wrong reasons as Kylian Mbappe comparison haunts Barcelona star
items.description:
The teenager still played a decisive role in the comeback, but his latest setback has drawn attention to an issue that could become increasingly significant as comparisons with Kylian Mbappe continue. 
Lamine Yamal endured a frustrating moment during Barcelona’s dramatic victory over Villarreal, adding another unwanted talking point to an otherwise impressive performance. The teenager still played a decisive role in the comeback, but his latest setback has drawn attention to an issue that could become increasingly significant as comparisons with Kylian Mbappe continue.



Barcelona produced an impressive second-half comeback to defeat Villarreal 3-2 at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday, despite falling two goals behind inside the opening seven minutes. Tajon Buchanan opened the scoring in the fifth minute before Tani Oluwaseyi doubled the visitors’ advantage just 128 seconds later.



Hansi Flick’s side struggled early on, with a makeshift defence featuring Frenkie de Jong at centre-back because of injuries to Andreas Christensen and Pau Cubarsi. Villarreal took full advantage, leaving the La Liga champions facing an uphill battle in front of their home supporters.



The Blaugrana eventually found their rhythm after the break, with Gerard Martin reducing the deficit in the 57th minute. Fermin Lopez then levelled the score following excellent work from Yamal, before Pau Navarro turned an Eric Garcia cross into his own net to complete the turnaround.









However, one first-half moment drew particular attention. After winning a penalty, Yamal stepped up to take responsibility but sent his effort against the right-hand post, missing an opportunity to bring Barcelona back into the contest earlier.



Yamal enters La Liga history for the wrong reason



The missed spot-kick carried a significant statistical consequence. According to figures highlighted by Spanish statistician Alexis, known as MisterChip, Yamal has now missed three of the seven penalties he has taken in La Liga, with two of those attempts striking the post.



At 19 years and 132 days old, he has become the youngest player in La Liga history to miss three penalties. He surpassed Fernando Torres, who reached the same unwanted milestone at 20 years and 64 days in 2004.



RankPlayerAge when missing third penaltyYear1.Lamine Yamal19 years, 132 days20262.Fernando Torres20 years, 64 days20043.López Ufarte20 years, 312 days19794.Lafuente21 years, 174 days1929Youngest players to miss three penalties in La Liga history



The historical list also includes Lopez Ufarte, who was 20 years and 312 days old when he missed his third penalty in 1979, and Lafuente, who reached the mark at 21 years and 174 days in 1929. Yamal’s record is particularly striking given how early in his senior career he has already taken responsibility from the spot.



Lamine Yamal of FC Barcelona looks on



Mbappe comparison adds another layer to the debate



Yamal’s penalty struggles have also invited comparisons with Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe, who has faced criticism over his own record from 12 yards. The Frenchman recently missed a penalty against Celta Vigo, failing to convert an opportunity that could have helped his team equalize.



RankPlayerPenalties missedAttemptsMiss rate1.Kylian Mbappe52321.7%2.Vedat Muriqi31030.0%2.Robert Lewandowski3742.9%Most La Liga penalties missed since the start of 2024–25



MisterChip also suggests that Mbappe has missed five of his 23 La Liga penalties since the beginning of the 2024-25 season, more than any other player in the competition over that period. Vedat Muriqi and Robert Lewandowski follow with three misses each.



PlayerPenalties missedAttemptsMiss rateKylian Mbappe52321.7%Lamine Yamal3742.9%Mbappe vs. Yamal: Penalty miss rates



The difference becomes more noticeable when looking at their respective conversion rates. Yamal has missed three of seven attempts, while the Frenchman has missed five of 23, giving the Barcelona teenager a considerably higher failure rate.

items.title: Getafe vs Atletico Madrid: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 LaLiga match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Getafe vs Atletico Madrid in the 2026-27 LaLiga. Getafe host Atletico Madrid in a LaLiga meeting between a side fighting to stop the bleeding at home and a visitor still chasing consistency on the road.
Getafe have dropped two of their last three, falling 0-2 to Villarreal on November 8 and 0-4 to Athletic on October 25, sandwiched around a 3-1 win over Sevilla on November 1. The heavy loss to Athletic exposed problems defensively, and the Villarreal result did nothing to settle those nerves. A home game against Atletico Madrid now carries real weight for Getafe as they try to steady themselves before the fixtures pile up.
Atletico Madrid also enter on a mixed run, losing 1-2 to Barcelona on November 8 after back-to-back wins over Levante on October 31 and Deportivo on October 24. Those two victories came by matching 2-0 and 1-0 scorelines, suggesting a team that can grind out results even without scoring freely. A win at Getafe would help Atletico Madrid answer questions raised by the Barcelona defeat and keep pace in the table.
Getafe confirmed lineup
Jose Bordalas sets Getafe up in a 3-4-1-2, with Dávid Soria in goal behind a back three of Sebastián Boselli, Zaid Romero and Andrés García. Dani Carvajal and Djené provide width as wing-backs, with Ramón Terrats and Orel Mangala holding the midfield and Johan Mojica pushing on from the back line. Martín Satriano and Enes Ünal lead the attack, with the pairing suggesting Bordalás wants a direct, physical approach against Atletico’s back line. Getafe are without Juanmi Jiménez, Chrisantus Uche and Nemanja Gudelj, all out, which thins their attacking and midfield options and puts more responsibility on Satriano and Ünal up front.
Getafe confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Dávid Soria, Dani Carvajal, Jean Ives Valou, Djené, Johan Mojica, Andrés García, Mario Martín, Orel Mangala, Ramón Terrats, Enes Ünal, Martín Satriano. Coach: José Bordalás.
Atletico Madrid confirmed lineup
Diego Simeone lines Atletico Madrid up in a 4-3-3, with Jan Oblak behind a back four of Marcos Llorente, Robin Le Normand, Dávid Hancko and Alex Grimaldo. Pablo Barrios, Koke and Johnny Cardoso make up a midfield built for control, while Giuliano Simeone, Julián Alvarez and Álex Baena offer pace and movement across the front line. That trio gives Atletico Madrid options to stretch Getafe’s back three and exploit space behind the wing-backs. Alejandro Grimaldo and Cristian Romero are both out, a notable loss on the defensive side that could test the depth of Atletico Madrid’s back line against a Getafe team set up to press and disrupt.
Atletico Madrid confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Jan Oblak, Marcos Llorente, Robin Le Normand, Dávid Hancko, Alex Grimaldo, Johnny Cardoso, Koke, Pablo Barrios, Giuliano Simeone, Julián Alvarez, Álex Baena. Coach: Diego Simeone.

items.title: AC Milan vs Frosinone: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Serie A match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for AC Milan vs Frosinone in the 2026-27 Serie A. Milan host Frosinone at San Siro with both sides fresh off contrasting midweek results, and this one carries real weight for the home side’s push up the table.
AC Milan arrive on the back of a 2-1 win over Genoa on November 8, which followed a 3-1 statement win over Inter on October 31. Those two results papered over a 2-4 loss to Bologna on October 28, and the Genoa win suggests the defending issues from that Bologna game have been addressed. A third straight win would keep Milan firmly in touch with the top of the table.
Frosinone come in off a 0-1 loss to Cagliari on November 7, a result that snapped the momentum built by a 2-0 win over Torino on November 1 and a 5-1 rout of Lecce on October 29. The Cagliari defeat was their first in three outings, and a positive result at San Siro would steady things after that setback. Points on the road against a team like Milan would be a strong marker for where Frosinone stand this season.
AC Milan confirmed lineup
Amorim sets Milan up in a 4-4-1-1 with Mike Maignan behind a back four of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Strahinja Pavlović and Sankhoun Diawara. Yunus Musah and Adrien Rabiot anchor the midfield, with Christian Pulisic and Diego Moreira providing width to support Luka Modrić just behind Gonçalo Ramos up top. There are no listed absences, so Amorim has his preferred group available, and the shape allows Modrić freedom to drift into pockets while Ramos leads the line alone.
AC Milan confirmed starting XI (4-4-1-1): Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara, Davide Bartesaghi, Yunus Musah, Adrien Rabiot, Christian Pulisic, Luka Modrić, Diego Moreira, Gonçalo Ramos. Coach: Ruben Amorim.
Frosinone confirmed lineup
Alvini goes with a 4-2-3-1 for Frosinone, with Lorenzo Palmisani in goal behind Anthony Oyono, Gabriele Calvani, Ilario Monterisi and Enzo Tchato. Patrizio Masini and Giacomo Calò sit as the double pivot, screening for an attacking trio of Romano Schmid, Farès Ghedjemis and Giorgi Kvernadze behind lone striker Daniel Bîrligea. With no absences reported, Alvini can field his full-strength setup, leaning on Kvernadze and Ghedjemis to combine around Bîrligea on the counter.
Frosinone confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Lorenzo Palmisani, Anthony Oyono, Gabriele Calvani, Ilario Monterisi, Enzo Tchato, Patrizio Masini, Romano Schmid, Giorgio Cittadini, Farès Ghedjemis, Giorgi Kvernadze, Giacomo Calò. Coach: Massimiliano Alvini.

items.title: Liverpool vs Manchester United: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Liverpool vs Manchester United in the 2026-27 Premier League. Anfield hosts another chapter of the oldest rivalry in English football, with Liverpool and Manchester United both looking to settle some nerves after uneven stretches through November.
Liverpool arrive off a 3-1 win over Crystal Palace on November 8, a result that followed a 0-1 loss to Arsenal and a 2-0 win over Albion in late October. The mix of results shows a team capable of bouncing back quickly after a setback. Three points here would put them back on more stable footing in the table.
Manchester United come in off a wild 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on November 8, sandwiched between a 0-2 loss to Chelsea on October 31 and a 0-3 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25. That stretch has produced just one point from three matches and no clean sheet in any of them. A result at Anfield would go a long way toward steadying a side short on momentum.
Liverpool confirmed lineup
Andoni Iraola projects a 4-2-3-1 built around pace and movement in behind, with Alexander Isak leading the line and support from Florian Wirtz and Cody Gakpo in the attacking midfield band. Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister anchor the double pivot, giving the side control through the middle, while Ronald Araujo and Jérémy Jacquet flank Virgil van Dijk in defense. The absences of Ryan Gravenberch, Jeremie Frimpong, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni, Amara Nallo and Hugo Ekitiké strip out depth across midfield, both fullback spots and the forward line, leaving Iraola with a leaner squad to rotate from if changes are needed.
Liverpool confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Alisson, Ronald Araujo, Jérémy Jacquet, Virgil Van Dijk, Miloš Kerkez, Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Alexis Mac Allister, Rio Ngumoha, Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola. Coach: Andoni Iraola.
Manchester United confirmed lineup
Mauricio Pochettino also sets up in a 4-2-3-1, with Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo pushed forward off Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo providing the attacking threat. Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo sit in front of a back four of Dalot, Martínez, Maguire and Yoro, a pairing tasked with controlling tempo against a Liverpool midfield that includes Wirtz and Mac Allister. United are without Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Šeško and Manuel Ugarte up front and through midfield, and Luke Shaw’s absence at left back adds to the defensive questions Pochettino has to manage heading into this one.
Manchester United confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Senne Lammens, Leny Yoro, Matthijs De Ligt, Lisandro Martínez, Diogo Dalot, Youri Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo, Patrick Dorgu, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha. Coach: Mauricio Pochettino.

items.title: Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami fall to Columbus Crew 3-0 in Game 1, putting their title defense on the brink
items.description:
Lionel Messi and Inter Miami open the defense of their MLS Cup title against Columbus Crew in Game 1 of the First Round, with all the build-up and live updates from Nu Stadium. 
Inter Miami‘s title defense got off to a nightmare start, as Columbus Crew won Game 1 of the First Round 3-0 at Nu Stadium and took a big step toward ending the reigning champions’ run. Gonzalo Tapia put the visitors in front early from the penalty spot, and Miami never found a way back into the series opener.



The hosts’ task got even harder just before halftime, when defender Gonzalo Lujan was sent off for a second yellow card in the 36th minute. Playing with ten men for more than half of the match, Miami lost control of the game, and Columbus took advantage of the extra space after the break.



Taha Habroune doubled the lead shortly after the restart, and Tapia added his second of the night to make it 3-0. From there, the Crew managed the game comfortably, while Lionel Messi and the rest of the attack could not create enough to threaten a comeback.



Inter Miami now face a very difficult position in a best-of-three series, with their season on the line. Game 2 is scheduled for Friday, November 27, in Columbus, where Miami must win to stay alive. If they do, Game 3 would be played in Miami on December 2, but another defeat would end their title defense.

items.title: How Inter Miami’s win, draw, or loss vs Columbus Crew could impact the 2026 MLS Playoffs First Round
items.description:
Game 1 at Nu Stadium could shape the entire First Round series, and each result, whether a win, a draw, or a loss, opens a different path for Inter Miami and Columbus Crew. 
Inter Miami begin the defense of their MLS Cup title when they host Columbus Crew in Game 1 of the first-round, best-of-three Eastern Conference series on Saturday at Nu Stadium. Lionel Messi‘s team enters as the No. 2 seed in the East, while the Crew arrive as the No. 7 seed, and the first side to win two games will move on to the Conference Semifinals.



The series follows a home-away-home format, so Inter Miami host Game 1, Columbus host Game 2 on Friday, November 27, and a decisive Game 3 would return to Miami on December 2.



Inter Miami arrive with Messi at the center of the plan after he won the 2026 MLS Golden Boot, the first player to do so in consecutive seasons. Miami finished the regular season with a 16-6-12 record, but the team lost some consistency after a strong start, with only one win in its last four games.



Columbus finished the regular season with a 14-15-5 record, but they arrive with momentum, carrying a four-game winning run, and they will try to pull off a big upset at Nu Stadium by taking the first game of the series.




It’s time for more. 🤜🤛 #MIAvCLB • @RoyalCaribbean pic.twitter.com/FDMsw4lO8V— Inter Miami CF (@InterMiamiCF) November 21, 2026




What happens if Inter Miami defeat Columbus Crew?



A win in Game 1 would put Inter Miami one victory away from the Conference Semifinals, with a chance to close the series in Columbus on November 27. If they advance, they will face the winner of the series between the No. 3 New England Revolution and the No. 6 Philadelphia Union in the Conference Semifinals, scheduled for December 5-6.


        


What happens if Inter Miami and Columbus Crew draw?



A draw is not an option in this round. If the score is level after 90 minutes, no extra time will be played and the match will go straight to a penalty shootout, with the winner receiving the victory in the series. Extra time only returns from the Conference Semifinals onward.



What happens if Inter Miami loose to Columbus Crew?



A defeat would leave Inter Miami trailing 1-0 and force them to win Game 2 in Columbus to take the series to a Game 3 in Miami. If they lose again, the series would end and their title defense would be over, since the loser of a best-of-three series is eliminated.

items.title: Why is Vinicius Junior not starting for Real Madrid vs Celta Vigo in 2026-27 LaLiga Matchday 13?
items.description:
Vinicius Junior returns for Real Madrid, but his place in Jose Mourinho's plans is not as clear as it once was. 
Vinicius Junior is back in contention for Real Madrid after serving his suspension, but he will not be in the starting lineup for Saturday’s LaLiga match against Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu.



The Brazilian winger is available again in the league, yet Jose Mourinho chose Yan Diomande to start in the position Vinicius usually occupies on the left. The decision stands out because it is the first game Vinicius could have played since the ban began.



The suspension, which covered four matches after the game against Villarreal, ended just as Vinicius came back from a strong international break, where he scored five goals for Brazil, including a brace against Japan and a hat-trick against Singapore.



Even so, Mourinho made it clear at his pre-match press conference that nobody has a guaranteed place. “He is an incredible player, we want him, we need him, but there are no players with privileges or who have to play by decree,” the coach said.




🏟️ ¡VOLVEMOS AL BERNABÉU!@HP pic.twitter.com/e1CIupwAiG— Real Madrid C.F. (@realmadrid) November 21, 2026




Part of the explanation lies in Diomande’s recent form. Starting with the Villarreal match, the Ivorian has played five straight league games, all of them as a left winger, including the four that Vinicius missed. He scored three goals and provided one assist as Real Madrid won all five.



The calendar is the other factor. Real Madrid face three matches in eight days, followed by trips to Real Sociedad and Athletic Bilbao in LaLiga and then Arsenal in the Champions League. In that context, Vinicius’s absence from the starting lineup looks less like a punishment and more like a way of managing minutes, and his role off the bench could be an important one.


        


Real Madrid’s confirmed lineup against Celta Vigo



Mourinho has made some decisions of his own for this game, leaving several starters on the bench: Federico Valverde, who returned from international duty with Uruguay on Thursday and had time for only one training session, starts on the bench, along with Aurelien Tchouameni, Marc Cucurella and Antonio Rudiger.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo misses a second straight penalty for Al Nassr: How many has Lionel Messi missed in 2026?
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo's latest penalty miss invites a look at how Lionel Messi has fared from the spot in 2026. 
Cristiano Ronaldo missed a penalty on Friday in Al Nassr’s 3-1 defeat at Al Ahli, his second in a row in the Saudi Pro League. The error brings back an obvious comparison with Lionel Messi, who also went through a difficult stretch from the spot this year, and the numbers show how close both players are.



Ronaldo’s miss came minutes after he had opened the scoring, when his effort struck the post, and it followed another failure from the spot against Neom on October 20, in a match Al Nassr still won 1-0.



The miss against Al Ahli was the first time he had failed on consecutive league penalties since joining the club in January 2023. Besides those two, Ronaldo also missed from the spot in a 3-1 victory over Al Fayha, so he has now failed three times in 2026, all of them in Saudi Pro League matches.



Messi has missed exactly three as well, and two of them came on the biggest stage. He failed against Austria at the World Cup and then saw goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir save his penalty against Egypt, in the 3-2 round of 16 victory. 



Lionel Messi reacts after missing a penalty vs Austria at the 2026 World Cup. (Getty Images)



His last miss came in mid-August, when the Inter Miami captain failed from the spot in a regular-season MLS match at Nashville, which Inter Miami went on to lose 4-1.



Ronaldo has scored one more penalty than Messi in 2026


        


Counting the penalties they have scored, the comparison tilts slightly toward Ronaldo. The Portuguese converted four in 2026: three in the Saudi Pro League plus one in Portugal’s 2-1 win over Croatia at the World Cup.



Messi, for his part, found the net three times, against Colorado in MLS, against Iceland in a friendly in June and against Benin in his farewell match with Argentina in October.



Messi holds an unwanted record at the World Cup



Messi’s misses are not limited to this year: he is the player with the most penalties missed in World Cup history. The Argentine has failed on four of the eight penalties he has taken in regulation time, missing against Iceland in 2018, Poland in 2022, and Austria and Egypt in 2026.



The two failures this year also made him the first player to miss more than one penalty in the same World Cup, excluding shootouts. Argentina won both matches anyway, but the one against Egypt was close: they were two goals down as late as the 79th minute before coming back to win 3-2. The other four penalties Messi has taken in the tournament were all scored at Qatar 2022, the final among them.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo wastes a big chance to close in on Ivan Toney at the top of the Saudi Pro League scoring chart
items.description:
A missed penalty at Al Ahli left Cristiano Ronaldo five goals behind Ivan Toney in the Saudi Pro League scoring race. 
Cristiano Ronaldo had the chance to take another step toward Ivan Toney in the Saudi Pro League scoring race on Friday, but a missed penalty left the gap exactly where it was.



The Portuguese forward scored for Al Nassr in Jeddah, yet Al Ahli came back to win 3-1, with Toney converting a penalty of his own to put the hosts ahead. The result keeps Ronaldo second in the scoring chart, behind the English striker who leads it.



The match, a postponed fixture from the ninth round, started well for the visitors. Ronaldo opened the scoring in the 14th minute after Samu Costa won the ball from Al Ahli’s build-up, and the 41-year-old finished into the far corner in his first game since retiring from the Portugal national team.



A few minutes later, Al Nassr were awarded a penalty for a foul inside the box, which gave Ronaldo a big chance to add to his tally. However, the Portuguese forward’s effort struck the post, and it was his second consecutive league penalty miss.



🚨BREAKING:Cristiano Ronaldo has broken the record for most missed penalties in football history, record previously held by Cristiano Ronaldo himself 😭😂 . pic.twitter.com/VFwK88RpuT— Johnny Cortes (@johnnycortes) November 20, 2026 



The miss proved costly, because Al Ahli took control from that point on. Galeno equalized with a long-range strike right at the end of the first half, Toney scored from the spot in the 71st minute after a VAR review, and Roger Ibanez headed in a third from a corner in the 75th.



Ronaldo is still Toney’s closest pursuer in the scoring chart



After Al Ahli’s win, Toney remains the outright leader of the Saudi Pro League scoring chart with 14 goals, while Cristiano Ronaldo is second with nine. Although the gap is still considerable, Al Nassr have 22 league matches left to play, so Ronaldo has time to close it.



Even so, Ronaldo’s hold on second place is not especially comfortable. Tijjani Reijnders of Al Qadsiah is third with eight, just one goal behind him, and three strikers are on seven: Alexandre Lacazette of Neom, Mateo Retegui of Al Qadsiah and Youssef En-Nesyri of Al Ittihad.



The missed penalty will stay as the image of the night for Ronaldo, but Al Nassr have little time to dwell on it. They return to action in the AFC Champions League Elite against Al Sadd on November 24, and then host Al Hazem in the league on November 28, a chance for the Portuguese forward to start cutting down the distance to Ivan Toney.

items.title: Newcastle vs Arsenal: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Newcastle vs Arsenal in the 2026-27 Premier League. Newcastle host Arsenal at St James’ Park with the visitors looking to keep pace at the top of the table and the home side trying to find more consistency in front of their own fans.
Newcastle come into this one off a 1-1 draw with Fulham last Saturday, a result that followed a 0-1 loss to Everton on November 2. Before that they beat Crystal Palace 2-0 on October 25, so the form has been mixed over the last three outings. A win here would steady things after back-to-back games without a victory.
Arsenal arrive on the back of three straight wins, starting with a 2-0 victory over Everton on October 24, then a 1-0 win at Liverpool on November 1, and most recently a 1-0 defeat of Hull on November 7. That run has them playing with real momentum heading into the trip to Newcastle. Another win would extend their unbeaten streak and keep the pressure on the teams above them.
Newcastle confirmed lineup
Jaissle sets Newcastle up in a 4-2-3-1, with Lewis Hall and Amar Dedić providing width from full back while Malick Thiaw and Dan Burn anchor the center of defense. Lewis Miley and Joe Willock sit as the double pivot, giving the team some control in midfield, and Nico González operates just behind William Osula as the central attacking midfielder. Jacob Murphy and Harvey Barnes flank the attack, offering pace on both sides. Newcastle are without Joelinton and Ewen Jaouen, both ruled out, which thins their options through the middle of the park.
Newcastle confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Lukáš Horníček, Amar Dedić, Malick Thiaw, Dan Burn, Lewis Hall, Lewis Miley, Joe Willock, Sean Steur, Jacob Murphy, William Osula, Harvey Barnes. Coach: Matthias Jaissle.
Arsenal confirmed lineup
Arteta also lines Arsenal up in a 4-2-3-1, with David Raya behind a back four of Jurriën Timber, Gabriel Magalhães, Ezri Konsa and Riccardo Calafiori. Declan Rice and Bruno Guimarães form the midfield pairing, screening the defense and supplying the attack. Martín Odegaard plays as the number 10 behind Kai Havertz, with Noni Madueke and Christos Tzolis providing width in the final third. Arsenal are missing Bukayo Saka, Louie Copley and Max Dowman, all ruled out, which removes some attacking depth from Arteta’s bench options.
Arsenal confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): David Raya, Jurriën Timber, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhães, Riccardo Calafiori, Bruno Guimarães, Martín Odegaard, Declan Rice, Noni Madueke, Kai Havertz, Eberechi Eze. Coach: Mikel Arteta.

items.title: Tottenham vs Ipswich Town: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Tottenham vs Ipswich Town in the 2026-27 Premier League. Tottenham host Ipswich Town in a Premier League fixture where both sides are looking to arrest recent slides in form.
Tottenham have mixed results lately. They beat Chelsea 2-0 on October 24 and followed that with a 2-0 win over Crystal Palace on October 31, but they then lost 0-1 to Leeds on November 7. A win here would put that defeat behind them and restore momentum at home.
Ipswich Town arrive on the back of three straight winless results. They drew 1-1 at Nottingham on October 23 and 2-2 with Hull on October 31, then lost 1-2 to Bournemouth on November 8. They need a positive result to stop the bleeding and ease the pressure building on the group.
Tottenham confirmed lineup
Roberto De Zerbi sets Tottenham up in a 4-2-3-1, with Antonín Kinský behind a back four of Pedro Porro, Jan-Paul van Hecke, Micky van de Ven and Andy Robertson. Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes sit as the double pivot, screening for an attacking line of Archie Gray, Mohammed Kudus and Omar Marmoush behind lone striker Dominic Solanke. The team is missing a significant number of attacking options, with Savinho, Mykhaylo Mudryk, Mathys Tel, Wilson Odobert, Xavi Simons and Richarlison all out, while Lucas Bergvall is absent in midfield and Tosin Adarabioyo is unavailable at the back. That depletion puts extra weight on Kudus, Marmoush and Solanke to create and finish chances.
Tottenham confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Antonín Kinský, Pedro Porro, Destiny Udogie, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mohammed Kudus, Conor Gallagher, Dominic Solanke, James Maddison, Lucá Williams-Barnett. Coach: Roberto De Zerbi.
Ipswich Town confirmed lineup
Gary O’Neill lines Ipswich Town up in a matching 4-2-3-1, with Christian Walton in goal behind Abdoul Ouattara, Dara O’Shea, Issa Diop and Leif Davis. Florentino Luís and Exequiel Palacios anchor midfield, supporting an attacking trio of Julio Enciso, Daizen Maeda and Jaden Philogene behind striker Emersonn. The team is close to full strength, with only Jack Taylor ruled out. That continuity should allow O’Neill to keep his structure settled as they look to find the cohesion that has been missing in recent draws.
Ipswich Town confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Christian Walton, Darnell Furlong, Leif Davis, Exequiel Palacios, Issa Diop, Dara O’Shea, Abdoul Ouattara, Saša Lukić, Zian Flemming, Julio Enciso, Daizen Maeda. Coach: Gary O’Neil.

items.title: FIFA confirms two challengers to Gianni Infantino in the 2027 presidential election
items.description:
Two challengers have entered the race to unseat Gianni Infantino, and a scrapped World Cup plan could shape how the federations vote. 
Gianni Infantino will not run unopposed when FIFA votes for its president next year. Two challengers have submitted candidacies to face him, which ends a run of two elections in which the Swiss executive was the only name on the ballot. It is the first time since his initial victory in 2016 that he will have to compete for the job.



The vote is scheduled for March 18, 2027, during the 77th FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco, where Infantino will face Philippe Diallo, who has led the French Football Federation since 2023, and Kohzo Tashima, a member of the FIFA Council since 2015 and honorary president of the Japan Football Association.



Diallo is reportedly the consensus candidate of UEFA’s 55 member associations, which gives him the backing of a continental bloc. Ramon Vega had also been part of the race as a third challenger, but he dropped out before the candidacies were confirmed.



The three candidates are not final yet, though. They now go to FIFA’s electoral committee, which has to review and admit them before they are put to the federations. The review is still pending, and the final list of candidates will only be known once it is complete.



FIFA President Gianni Infantino holds the FIFA World Cup trophy. (Getty Images)



The contrast with Infantino’s earlier elections is sharp. In 2016, he faced four rivals and needed a second round to defeat Sheikh Salman of Bahrain, 115 votes to 88. He was then reelected by acclamation in 2019 and again in 2023, but this time he will have to win a contested vote if he wants to stay in charge of FIFA.



A scrapped World Cup stake sale could weigh against Infantino


        


The biggest controversy hanging over Infantino’s reelection bid is FIFA’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to outside investors, an idea tied to a project known as FIFA Forward Enterprise.



The proposal was withdrawn after it drew criticism, and Infantino went as far as apologizing for it. Even so, the episode appears to be one of the main reasons his rivals decided to step forward.



That apology could work against him when the federations vote in Rabat. Diallo and Tashima now have a ready-made argument that the FIFA leadership needs a change of direction, and the backing of UEFA’s associations behind Diallo makes that message harder to ignore. Whether the controversy is enough to cost Infantino votes remains an open question, since the ballot is secret and he has won every previous election.

items.title: Al Ahli vs Al Nassr: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Al Ahli vs Al Nassr in the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League. Al Ahli host Al Nassr in a 2026-27 Saudi Pro League fixture that pits two sides coming off very different recent scorelines, with goals flying in at both ends over the past few weeks.
Al Ahli were beaten 6-1 by Al Shabab on October 30, a heavy loss that followed wins of 4-1 over Al Khaleej on October 23 and 3-2 over Al-Fayha on October 19. That run shows a team capable of scoring freely but also prone to conceding in bunches, and bouncing back quickly from the Al Shabab result matters a great deal for Marino Pušić’s group. A home game against a title rival is the sort of fixture that can either steady the ship or deepen the wobble.
Al Nassr arrive in much better form, having won 5-3 against Al Kholood on October 29 after previous victories of 3-1 over Al-Faisaly on October 23 and 1-0 against Neom SC on October 20. Three straight wins, each with goals involved except the Neom SC game, point to a team hitting a consistent attacking stride. Keeping that momentum intact on the road would send a strong signal to the rest of the league.
Al Ahli confirmed lineup
Marino Pušić sets Al Ahli up in a 4-2-3-1 with Édouard Mendy behind a back four of Saeed Baattia, Mohammed Sulaiman, Roger Ibañez and Abubacarr Sedi Kinteh. Artem Bondarenko and Eduard Spertsyan sit in front of that defense, screening for a attacking line of Valentin Atangana Edoa, Francisco Trincão and Wenderson Galeno behind lone striker Ivan Toney. There are no absences listed, so Pušić has his full projected group available, which will matter after conceding six goals in the last outing and needing more control in midfield.
Al Ahli confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Édouard Mendy, Saeed Baattia, Merih Demiral, Roger Ibañez, Saad Balobaid, Ziyad Al-Johani, Eduard Spertsyan, Valentin Atangana Edoa, Francisco Trincão, Ivan Toney, Wenderson Galeno. Coach: Marino Pušić.
Al Nassr confirmed lineup
Ange Postecoglou lines Al Nassr up in a 4-4-1-1, with Bento Krepski in goal protected by Nawaf Al-Boushail, Abdulelah Al Amri, Iñigo Martínez and Awad Aman. Ayman Yahya, Ângelo Gabriel, João Félix and Samu make up the midfield four, feeding Sadio Mané in support of Cristiano Ronaldo at the top of the shape. With no absences listed, Postecoglou can pick his strongest projected XI, and the Ronaldo-Mané pairing up front looks suited to exploiting a defense that has leaked goals recently.
Al Nassr confirmed starting XI (4-4-1-1): Bento Krepski, Nawaf Al-Boushail, Mohamed Simakan, Iñigo Martínez, Awad Aman, Abdullah Al-Hamdan, Ângelo Gabriel, João Félix, Samu, Abdullah Al-Khaibari, Cristiano Ronaldo. Coach: Ange Postecoglou.

items.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
items.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegatedThe Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged.Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. items.title: Antoine Griezmann claims an MLS award that slipped away from Lionel Messi in 2023
items.description:
Antoine Griezmann has earned an MLS honor that Lionel Messi came close to winning in 2023. 
Antoine Griezmann has barely settled into Major League Soccer, and he already has an individual honor to his name, one that even Lionel Messi did not win. The French forward was voted the league’s best newcomer after a standout first season with Orlando City.



MLS made it official this week: Griezmann is the 2026 Newcomer of the Year. The former Atletico Madrid forward arrived at Orlando City in March but did not take the field until July, and from then on his impact was immediate. He finished the regular season with 14 goals and eight assists, a club-best 22 goal contributions.



He needed only 15 games to reach 20 goal contributions, the second-fastest mark in league history, and he was involved in 32.9% of Orlando’s 63 goals, which helped the team reach the playoffs as the Eastern Conference’s No. 8 seed.



With 51.02% of the votes, he finished well ahead of Houston’s Guilherme (25.12%) and Sporting Kansas City’s Andre Luiz (6.19%), and he led in all three groups of voters: players, media and clubs.




The new guys lit up the league this year. 🔥The voters' choice? Antoine Griezmann. 🗳️ pic.twitter.com/0BZatgeSgr— Major League Soccer (@MLS) November 17, 2026




Messi came close to winning it in 2023



Messi will never have another chance to win this award, since it recognizes players in their first year in MLS, but he came close to taking it in 2023. The Argentine arrived at Inter Miami that summer and finished second in the voting with 27.28%, behind Atlanta United’s Giorgos Giakoumakis, who received 45.78%.


        


Messi did win the players’ vote that year, with 35.54%, narrowly ahead of Giakoumakis, who got 34.34%. But the media and club votes tilted the balance toward the Greek striker, who took the award, and Eduard Lowen of St. Louis City finished third with 15.44%.



With the playoffs about to begin, Griezmann will try to turn an award-winning debut into a deeper run with Orlando City, while Messi and Inter Miami arrive as defending champions. Their paths could keep crossing in the conversation, even if only one of them will have this particular trophy on the shelf.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement plans emerge as Real Madrid could welcome Portugal star back for special occasion
items.description:
Although the Portugal legend remains focused on his future with Al-Nassr, reports suggest discussions about a more fitting farewell are already taking shape, with some familiar faces potentially involved. 
Cristiano Ronaldo‘s international retirement has raised fresh questions about how one of soccer’s greatest careers will eventually come to an end. Although the Portugal legend remains focused on his future with Al-Nassr, reports suggest discussions about a more fitting farewell are already taking shape, with some familiar faces potentially involved.



The 41-year-old still has major ambitions before considering retirement from the game altogether. However, his departure from international soccer has left unfinished business, particularly after the difficult circumstances surrounding his final months with Portugal.



According to The Athletic, people close to Ronaldo say his immediate sporting priority is reaching 1,000 career goals. He reportedly has 985 goals to his name, leaving him 15 short of the historic milestone as he continues playing for Al-Nassr.



Ronaldo has previously indicated that he could consider retiring after the Saudi Pro League season next June. Beyond the goalscoring target, however, those familiar with his plans suggest he has relatively few other sporting ambitions before eventually bringing his playing career to a close.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr celebrates a goal.



Portugal hopes to give its former captain proper send-off



Ronaldo announced his international retirement on November 5, 2026, ending a 23-year career with Portugal. He finished with 234 appearances and 146 goals, both men’s international records, while winning Euro 2016 and two Nations League titles.



His departure came after a difficult period involving head coach Jorge Jesus, with their disagreement over Ronaldo’s unused substitute appearance against Norway contributing to the breakdown in their relationship. The former captain’s last appearance came in September’s 1-0 victory over Wales, meaning he never received a proper farewell in front of Portugal supporters.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal.



The Athletic adds there is still hope on both sides that the situation can eventually be resolved. The report suggests that “in time, all sides are hopeful they can arrange a formal farewell game” to recognize Ronaldo’s contribution to Portuguese soccer, although “a little more time may be needed for the freshest of wounds to fully heal.”



Real Madrid could play role as well



Beyond a potential Portugal tribute, Ronaldo could receive a separate farewell involving some of his former clubs, with Real Madrid among those mentioned. Such an occasion would offer an opportunity to celebrate his achievements across club soccer before he eventually retires altogether, the report reveals.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Real Madrid CF holds the Ballon d’Or 2013



His connection with Real Madrid makes the possibility particularly significant. Ronaldo spent nine seasons at the Santiago Bernabéu between 2009 and 2018, scoring 451 goals in 438 appearances and becoming the club’s all-time leading goalscorer. He also helped Real Madrid win four Champions League titles, two La Liga championships and numerous other trophies. 



His contribution to the club’s historic European dominance cemented his place among its greatest-ever players. Ronaldo joined Real Madrid from Manchester United in 2009 for a then-world-record $103 million transfer fee. During his time in Spain, he won four Ballons d’Or and established several scoring records, including the remarkable 17-goal Champions League campaign in 2013-14.









His departure in 2018 brought an end to one of the most successful individual spells in the club’s history, as he moved to Juventus before later returning to Manchester United and eventually joining Al-Nassr. A farewell involving Los Blancos would therefore provide a fitting opportunity to celebrate the achievements that defined much of his career.

items.title: Christian Pulisic reveals what Mauricio Pochettino told USMNT before Man Utd move and singles out what U.S. Soccer must demand from his successor
items.description:
The result secured another important achievement for the Americans, while Pulisic's outstanding performance provided a memorable moment in the Argentine coach's farewell. 
Christian Pulisic and Mauricio Pochettino ended their time together with the United States men’s national team on a high after a convincing victory over Haiti in Cincinnati. The result secured another important achievement for the Americans, while Pulisic’s outstanding performance provided a memorable moment in the Argentine coach’s farewell.



The Milan forward also reflected on the progress made during Pochettino’s tenure and the direction the national team should take next. With the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager preparing for a new challenge at Manchester United, attention is already turning towards the person who will replace him.



Pulisic opened the scoring in the 25th minute with an acrobatic bicycle kick after Weston McKennie delivered a cross towards the far post. The finish was particularly memorable because it was the first bicycle kick Pulisic had scored in his professional or international career. “I’d never scored a goal like that before. It was special. Weston crossed the ball, and it was really the only thing I could do, so I thought I had to give it a go. It was really nice to see the ball go in,” Pulisic said after the match.



The goal was his 36th for the United States, while McKennie later assisted 18-year-old Julian Hall for the second goal in the 43rd minute. The 2-0 victory completed an 8-0 aggregate win over Haiti, sending the United States into the Concacaf Nations League Finals scheduled for March 2027. The Americans also secured qualification for the 2027 Gold Cup and extended their winning run to six matches.



EVERY ANGLE OF THE PULISIC BICYCLE KICK 🎥 pic.twitter.com/jFSFZx5Wan— U.S. Soccer Men’s National Team (@USMNT) November 18, 2026



Pochettino finished his tenure with a record of 23 wins, two draws, and 12 defeats, having taken charge in October 2024. His departure was an emotional occasion, with the coach embracing his players and receiving a standing ovation from the crowd at TQL Stadium.



Play Country Roads. pic.twitter.com/gHgVmlIZ9J— U.S. Soccer Men’s National Team (@USMNT) November 18, 2026



Pulisic reveals Pochettino’s final message to the USMNT



Pulisic offered an insight into what the Argentine told the squad before leaving for England to take over at Manchester United. Rather than focusing on individual performances or immediate results, Pochettino’s farewell message centered on the culture and foundations built during his time with the national team.



“Simply that we have a really extraordinary culture. We’ve built something really special and have a bright future ahead of us. And to keep it going, letting the rest of the team support us,” Pulisic revealed.



Christian Pulisic on his bicycle kick, Pochettino, and Julian Hall pic.twitter.com/F3ITKV4yeR— TopBin90 (@Topbin90) November 18, 2026



The forward believes the United States has made meaningful progress under the former Paris Saint-Germain manager and should be confident about what lies ahead. “We’re in a good place. I mean, I think the team have improved. I think there’s a good culture within the group and I think we should be really excited about the future,” he added.



Pochettino also expressed confidence in the squad’s potential, pointing to the combination of experienced internationals and emerging young players. “I am sure that this group of players will achieve big things in the future. I have no doubt,” he told reporters.



Pulisic outlines what Pochettino’s successor must deliver



With Pochettino moving to Manchester United, U.S. Soccer must now find a manager capable of maintaining the progress made during his tenure. Pulisic acknowledged that the identity of the next coach matters, even though the players have no say in the appointment.



USMNT celebrate vs Mexico



“I mean, it’s not that it doesn’t matter. In the end, it’s not our choice as players. Whoever comes in, we hope they know how to make the most of the things we do very well and can lead us in a good direction,” he explained.



U.S. Soccer chief executive J.T. Batson has also highlighted the qualities the federation will prioritize when choosing a successor. Speaking before the Haiti match, Batson said the next appointment must care about youth development, the youth national team programs, relationships with clubs, and the wider success of the federation.

items.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
items.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quicklyIt’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it.But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio. From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...
